notes.1ai: Most candidates were able to give the number of legs as a feature. Many were unable to supply a second feature that was visible in the photograph.
notes.1aii: Few candidates answered this question correctly. The question was misread so that candidates tried to name a classification grouping that was within the animal kingdom.
notes.1bi: Most candidates understood that an adaptive feature helps an organism survive, but few candidates were able to state the full definition of an adaptive feature.
notes.1bii: Many excellent answers were seen for this question.
notes.2a: Most candidates were able to correctly insert names and functions into the table.
notes.2bi: Most candidates successfully named a cell found in plant cells but not in animal cells.
notes.2bii: Generally, a well answered question. The question needed to be read carefully in its entirety so that the named structure is found in both animal and plant cells.
notes.2c: Candidates were asked to name the cell and describe how it is adapted to its function. Most candidates identified the type of cell and then described how its large surface area helped it to absorb water and mineral ions. Some candidates gave transport of water as a function, but that is a function of the xylem.
notes.3a: This was a demanding question for many candidates. Many found it difficult to work out which structure represented the enzyme. The substrate was the structure that broke down into two products, therefore the remaining structure must be the enzyme.
notes.3b: This question was answered well. Many candidates understood that enzymes are catalysts, but some confused breaking down and speeding up.
notes.3ci: There was uncertainty over the enzyme that removes fat stains, and many selected an enzyme other than lipase.
notes.3cii: Some candidates found it difficult to describe enzyme-substrate specificity and apply this to the context in the question. Most incorrectly suggested that more enzyme would be better.
notes.3di: and (ii) Most candidates correctly read and recorded data from the graph.
notes.3diii: Few candidates noticed that the question asked what happens to the enzyme itself. Most answers were about the change in the time taken to remove a stain.
notes.4ai: Few candidates gave cheese as a source of calcium.
notes.4aii: A well answered question with many selecting two correct statements.
notes.4aiii: Although most candidates understood the importance of calcium for bones and teeth, some thought it was needed for an active lifestyle.
notes.4b: There was some uncertainty over this question. The most common incorrect responses were that scurvy is caused by a lack of iron or vitamin D and that rickets is caused by a lack of iron.
notes.4ci: Almost all candidates could name a dietary source of fibre.
notes.4cii: Some candidates confused excretion and egestion. The most common correct answer was to prevent constipation. Some candidates, who perhaps do not understand what fibre is, gave a vague answer, such as to keep healthy.
notes.4di: Many candidates correctly stated part D as the site of egestion.
notes.4dii: Many candidates correctly gave part C for the absorption of water, but few remembered that the small intestine, E , also absorbs water.
notes.5a: Candidates that noted the question referred to humans generally filled in all the gaps correctly.
notes.5b: Some candidates misread the question and gave lactic acid as an answer. The question asked for anaerobic respiration in yeast.
notes.6a: This question starts by describing a sense organ and its stimulus. Candidates were asked to state three other stimuli. Most candidates answered with the names of sense organs.
notes.6bi: This question was not well answered. Candidates should look closely at the part of the eye indicated by the end of the label line, so that the correct part can be named. A common mistake was to give lens for pupil.
notes.6bii: Few candidates knew the location of the blind spot.
notes.6ci: Some candidates found this question demanding and confused refraction with reflection. Most understood that impulses go to the brain.
notes.6cii: Dilation, or the pupil getting bigger, was correctly stated by most candidates. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2023
notes.7a: This question was well answered, even though it could have been difficult to describe the selection of a feature which can only be seen in females. Candidates were able to describe selecting both males and females for breeding. Many also went on to describe how this would continue through many generations.
notes.7b: Candidates often did not give responses that were specific to intensive farming. Thinking about how extensive farming compares with intensive farming might have helped them to find advantages. Unqualified responses about pollution or reduction in pathogens could also apply to extensive farming.
notes.8a: Candidates gave detailed descriptions about the roles of mitochondria and the acrosome in sperm cells. However, some confused the acrosome and mitochondria. If the word ‘it’ is used it must be clear which is being referred to. Energy release must be referred to correctly.
notes.8b: Most candidates were able to compare the relative size of an egg cell and a sperm cell and describe the numbers produced. Few candidates understood that motility refers to the ability to move independently.
notes.8c: Good attempts were made on this calculation. Candidates needed to convert numbers to the same format (e.g. 1 500 000 and 350 000) before inserting them into a suitable equation. The answer then needed to be given to one decimal place. Working must be shown so that credit can be given even if an error is made in the calculation.
notes.8di: Some candidates correctly identified the amniotic sac.
notes.8dii: Most candidates understood that R is the umbilical cord and that it connects mother and fetus, but many were unclear about what travels in the umbilical cord. Correct terms should be used as food does not travel in the cord. There were good answers for the role of amniotic fluid.
notes.8diii: Most candidates successfully described the functions of the placenta. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2023
